title: Making a Beat Out of a Broken Rhodes
creator: Dev Malhotra
description:
Found a Rhodes Mark I on the curb with half its tines dead. Made a beat out of what was left.

Everything recorded into a Tascam 388, then into Ableton for chopping.
No plugins on the drums except a bit of tape saturation.

The finished beat is at the end of the video.

#beatmaking #rhodes #lofi

sentences.t: So, this thing was sitting on the curb two streets from my place with a sign that said free, works kind of.
It's a Rhodes Mark one, and works kind of was very generous.
About a third of the keys don't make any sound at all, and the ones that do sound like they're underwater.
Which, for what we're doing today, is perfect.
I'm not fixing it, I'm making a beat out of whatever is still alive in here.
First thing, I'm just going to play every key and write down which ones work.
Okay, low E, dead, F, dead, F sharp, oh, that one's gorgeous actually, listen to that.
It's got this wobble because the tine is bent, it's like a built in chorus.
So I've got a weird little scale of maybe twelve notes that work, and none of them are in the same key, which is fun.
I'm going to record a few minutes of just noodling on those notes straight into the tape machine.
The Tascam adds a little hiss and squash that I really like with old keys.
Then into Ableton, and I chop it up, I'm looking for two or three seconds that loop on their own.
This bit, hear that, the little stumble at the end, that's the hook, that's the whole beat right there.
Pitch it down two semitones so it sits a bit darker.
Now drums, and I'm doing something a bit silly, I'm recording the drums on the Rhodes too.
If you knock on the side of the case it goes thunk, which is a kick drum if you squint.
The lid closing is a snare, and the sustain pedal squeaking is my hi hat, I'm not kidding.
A bit of saturation, a little compression, and suddenly it's a drum kit.
I love this stuff, this is the part of making music that feels like playing with Lego.
And honestly I needed a session like this, because the last month has been all client work.
I scored a Volvo commercial, the one with the family driving up the coast, that's me on the soundtrack.
It was the first time an agency hired me for something that big, and they were lovely, but it was intense.
Forty one revisions on a sixty second cue, because every time they recut the picture the music had to move.
At one point the note was make the piano feel more Swedish, and I still don't know what that means.
That job paid for the tape machine, so in a way it paid for this video too, which is nice.
But after six weeks of somebody else's brief, I just wanted to make something ugly and fun for myself.
Okay, bass, I'm playing a bass line on the lowest working key, which is a G, ish.
Really simple, just following the root of the chop.
Some vinyl crackle, a bit of room reverb on the whole thing, and a filter that opens up in the second half.
Let me arrange it real quick, intro with just the keys, drums come in at bar five, bass at bar nine.
Drop everything out for two bars, and then bring it all back with the filter open.
That's the trick that makes a loop feel like a song, take it away so people miss it.
Alright, I think it's done, or done enough.
Let me know in the comments what you'd call it, because I've been calling it curb piano and that can't be the name.
Here it is, the whole thing, start to finish, made from a broken keyboard somebody threw away.
Thanks for watching, and if you see a free piano on the street, give it a chance.
